title: Composition of projective-bundle morphisms over a qcqs base
statement: Let $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Suppose $C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme, def-weil-pbc-scheme-conventions]. If $f$ and $g$ are projective in the projective-bundle sense [def-trf-projective-bundle-morphism], then $g\circ f:A\to C$ is projective in the same sense.

proof.text: For each of $f:A\to B$ and $g:B\to C$, apply [lem-trf-projective-bundle-proper] to its assumed projective-bundle factorization, obtaining properness. Apply [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-relative-ample] separately to these same two morphisms. It supplies finite type of each map and invertible modules $L$ on $A$ and $M$ on $B$ that are respectively $f$-ample and $g$-ample. These are precisely the finite-type and relative-ampleness conditions used in the next step. Neither application requires quasi-compactness or quasi-separatedness of $B$.

source.place: Tag 0C4P (lemma-composition-projective), first sentence; projective implies quasi-projective by 07RL (lemma-projective-quasi-projective), and proper by 01WC (lemma-locally-projective-proper).

proof.text: Set $h=g\circ f:A\to C$. The properness of $f$ and $g$ from Step 1 gives properness of $h$ by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-composition]. For relative ampleness apply [lem-sfb-quasiprojective-qc-composition] with $X=A$, $Y=B$, $S=C$ and the modules $L,M$ of Step 1: both maps are of finite type, their respective relative-ampleness hypotheses hold, and the final base $C$ is quasi-compact by the item hypothesis. The conclusion gives finite type of $h$ and an invertible module $N$ on $A$ that is $h$-relatively ample. No quasi-separatedness of $B$ or global finite-projective-space embedding is used.

source.place: Tag 0C4P (lemma-composition-projective), second sentence; proper composition 01W3 (lemma-composition-proper) and quasi-projective composition 0C4M (lemma-composition-quasi-projective).

proof.text: Use [lem-sfb-proper-relative-ample-projective-bundle] for $h:A\to C$ and $N$. Step 2 supplies properness of $h$ and relative ampleness of the invertible module $N$. The item assumes exactly the remaining hypotheses, namely that $C$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. Consequently $A$ embeds as a closed subscheme of a projective bundle associated to a finite-type quasi-coherent module on $C$. This is projectivity in the stipulated projective-bundle sense and proves the conclusion.

source.place: Tag 0C4P (lemma-composition-projective), last sentence; implication (1) of 0BCL (lemma-projective-is-quasi-projective-proper), from proper and quasi-projective to projective.
